So there're several meta questions worth discussing:

  • Do we host the agreement text here as a post? Or on some sort of wiki? Or as a gitbook? Or just as a GitHub Page?
  • Do we version it somehow? Surely there will be changes. It would be great to use Semantic Versioning.
  • Do we have some sort of committee? Or are you our benevolent dictator, @Mumberthrax? How do we resolve conflicts if they appear?
  • How and where do we store signs? In the document itself? Is there some sort of specialized tool/service for this? Because having even 100+ signs in the main text sounds kinda messy to me.

I'm sorry that I missed this post previously. I hadn't considered that people would already be posting here so I haven't been checking the sub, and the admins have not yet remedied the bug with username pings in text-posts not working. :P

Here are my thoughts on the questions you brought up:

  1. I'm open to anything. My current plan is to host the document on github as a file. https://github.com/Mumberthrax/CivilVoatersAgreement/blob/master/CivilVoatersAgreement.md It could be pasted into a text-post here too, since both github and voat use markdown (more or less) the formatting ought to transfer without much fuss. We could possibly set it up with a github page I suppose, but I am not a web developer so I'm uncertain what is possible there or how to do that effectively. I've not ever heard of gitbook before, but it looks interesting. I'd need to look into that more to understand how it works or how it might be utilized in this project.

  2. Yes! Definitely versioning systems are going to be vital here so that if the document is changed people who signed an earlier version aren't compelled to have that signature transferred to something they don't explicitly agree with. I think the use of Semantic Versioning could be very useful. Thank you for sharing that link.

    I am envisioning something like this:

    • I'll compile and edit a rough draft version, solicit feedback, and edit it on my own based on feedback. The result will be a "beta" version of the agreement, which anyone can sign if they want to.
    • One to two months later I'll attempt to host a "constitutional convention" of sorts where everyone all over voat is invited to participate in discussing changes to the version of the document that I am maintaining (because the document is permissively licensed, anyone may also copy it and make their own version).
    • After the first convention, I would title the resulting document as v.1.0, and give it an adorable mnemonic name like Ubuntu uses ("Adept Alligator" or something. maybe have a little contest for names). This would further facilitate easier remembering of which version people signed, and might itself provide value as the source for characters in some kind of comics or cartoons, enriching Voat culture. or not. Just a thought.
    • I had been thinking that subsequent conventions, which would happen every three months maybe (maybe less frequently) would result in new version names, such as 2.0 (Brilliant Bat or something), 3.0 (Carmine Cuttlefish? :P ), etc. This would naturally conflict with Semantic Versioning. So it's something that would need to be figured out.

  3. Currently I'm the benevolent dictator so far as I'm aware for this implementation of the Civil Voaters' Agreement. I would like to see a committee of some sort in the future to have a democratic stewardship of the process, and that is not yet a level of bureaucracy that I am comfortable dealing with.

    For the time being the liberty to fork the document and maintain one's own version if one is unhappy with my stewardship is the solution I think has the best balance of freedom and ease of use, which permits focus to be on improving the document itself rather than progress being hampered by committee squabbling or inaction or any number of maladies that such executive committees can fall victim to if established on infirm ground. Once a solid template has been established through which the democratic authorship of the agreement can be administrated, then I'd be comfortable relinquishing my stewardship role for this branch of the document. I'm happy though to accept any assistance from others, opinions and suggestions. I welcome it.

  4. I am not certain about this. I think it would be neat if we could find a supercool way to do it in a way that is very slick and beautiful, and I'm okay with not having that. My current plan is at the very least, when there is a version of the document that is ready for signatures, it would be posted into a text-post here, and people would sign it by making a comment with their account saying some affirmation of their agreement "I agree with this!" or "+1" or "choo choo, all on the CVA karma train! (this is my signature :P)". Yeah it will be a bit messy. That's ok in my opinion. I like this method because it is intimately tied to the website itself - it's on Voat, not some third party thing. I'd very much like to keep this as intimately associated to Voat as a cultural artifact as possible.

    What would be really awesome is if atko or puttitout made a special page for it here on voat, where anyone could sign, leave a comment, etc. and their names would be in a nice clean list and comments would be visible on the side or something. That way it would still retain that familiarity and closeness with the site itself. Maybe if this becomes as popular as I hope it does, that could happen.

    But! If anyone does find some site which can do this in an elegant functional way, then I'd definitely like to hear about it and check it out.

Edit: accidentally triple-posted this comment because it told me "You are doing that too fast. Please wait 30 seconds before trying again." o_o

Thanks for the replies!

About the last point, the sign storage. I just realized that we better not store them in the document on GitHub, because that would mean either

  • A. You need to deanon and make a Pull Request with your username from your GitHub account, or
  • B. You need to PM, well, you, and then wait till you update the list, which is even more painful, especially for you.

What I think we can do is wait till the Voat API goes public and host a simple website somewhere where you can log in using Voat, click a button, and the site will save your sign in a database. There should also be another button to un-sign, of course.

There're tons of options to do that for free. Most notably, we can create a free 500Mb database on MongoLab, a static page on GitHub and do everything on the client side, only storing usernames in the db. I can arrange that, I'm a webdev.

I hope this isn't quadruple posting...

I definitely wouldn't want signatures to be done through PRs as that would be even more messy than leaving a comment on a release post. github has a few ways of leaving comments on a project, but I don't want people to have to create a github account in order to sign. ideally signing should be easy, the way to do it should be obvious to the person wanting to sign, and it should require no additional work for a moderator to process.

Using a github page and MongoLab database sounds pretty nifty. If the pending Voat API can be used, all the better. If you're interested in putting something together for it, that could be cool - but don't feel obligated to.

I suppose what I'd want to see in any sort of custom page for it is:

  1. the latest version of this branch of the agreement
  2. the list of signatories
  3. links to alternate versions and signatures
  4. a button to click to remove your signature
  5. links to related information such as an intro document, or details on how to propose changes or be involved in the democratic review
  6. Some pleasant styling

Back when I was 15, I had to attend boarding school. My roommate was an obese girl, almost 240 pounds, also 15 years old. This girl was stuffing her face 24/7, I shit you not. Even during the night, she would wake up and start eating chocolate or drink soda. It was pretty much like living with a pig, and our room was tiny. My dad was born with diabetes, and my doctor told me I would get it too, if I didn't watch my sugar intake (not really the way it works, but I was a dumb teen, cut me some slack) Generally I didn't snack much on anything besides vegetables. My pig of a roommate didn't believe this. She thought it was something I had made up because I didn't want to share my snacks with her, and she was pretty furious about it. Her logic about this was really shitty, like because she didn't like the taster of water, she couldn't imagine anyone else would drink anything besides soda. She told me more than once, the day she found my secret stash, she would eat/drink it all, and she started going through my stuff when I wasn't in the room. About 4 months in, I had to do a project in biology about plants, but unfortunately I was pretty clueless bout how to even keep a plant alive. During the following weekend, I asked my plant-lover mom about it, and she told me I should love it, water it and give it some fertilizer. At the time, she made her own fertilizer and she told me she would pour some in a bottle and put it in my bag, then I could use it on my own plant. Sunday evening I had forgotten everything about it, and when I arrived back at the boarding school, I tossed the bag on my bed and went to the bathroom to do my business and take a shower. When I get back to my room, I found miss piggy, my lovely roommate, puking all over the floor. On the floor laid the empty soda bottle from my bag, I had forgotten all about. Turn out she had raided my bag the moment I was out of the room. When she found the soda bottle, she apparently tried to drink it, thinking it was ordinary soda I was hiding from her. Not only did she get punished because she had finally been caught stealing red-handed and had to clean up the mess herself, she was sent home shortly after, because she kept telling everyone I had tried to poison her. About a month later I asked my mom what exactly the ingredients of her fertilizer consisted of, and she told me it's was wet horse manure mixed with boiled, gemfree water.

TL;DR - Greedy roommate thinks I am hiding snacks from her, and gets angry. Drinks fertilizer, because she confuses it for soda.
